text_pages.text:
MIZORAM PUBLIC SERVICE COMMISSION
COMPETITIVE EXAMINATIONS FOR RECRUITMENT TO THE POST OF
GEOLOGIST JUNIOR UNDER COMMERCE & INDUSTRIES DEPARTMENT,
GOVERNMENT OF MIZORAM, NOVEMBER, 2022
GENERAL ENGLISH PAPER - II
Time Allowed : 2 hours
Full Marks : 100
All questions carry equal mark of 1 each.
Attempt all questions.
Directions (Question No. 1 - 10): Choose the correct answer from the options given:
1. What is the collective noun from the following sentence:
He was part of the film crew.
(a) He
(b) Film
(c) Crew
(d) None of the above
2. Pick out the proper noun from the following sentence:
Rajiya led the class to the stadium.
(a) Rajiya
(b) Class
(c) Stadium
(d) Led
3. Pick out the pronouns from the following sentence:
He came to pick her up all by himself.
(a) He, her
(b) He, her, himself
(c) He
(d) Her
4. Which of the following sentence has a preposition.
(a) The cat ran.
(b) We will talk.
(c) Keep working hard.
(d) She asked about the dog.
5. Identify the sentence that does not have an Adjective.
(a) The huge dog barked.
(b) The girl had a pink scarf.
(c) Can you play tennis?
(d) Children had hot chocolate milk.
6. Identify the sentence that has an adverb in it:
(a) I am travelling in a fast train.
(b) The train runs fast.
(c) I love red dresses.
(d) Those are beautiful paintings.
7. Which sentence in the following does not have a conjunction:
(a) She is lazy but intelligent.
(b) Rana, Mohit and Lily are on leave.
(c) If it rains, do not come.
(d) The boy with blue coloured hair is here.
8. Pick out a sentence from the following showing happiness.
(a) Hurrah! We have won the match.
(b) Alas! My mother is no more.
(c) What a lovely child she is!
(d) Oh! That’s my cousin.
9. Pick out the correct part of speech for the word in italics in the sentence given below:
This a hard metal.
(a) Adverb
(b) Adjective
(c) Noun
(d) Preposition

- 2 -
10. Pick out the correct part of speech for the word in italics in the sentence given below:
Delhi is the capital of India.
(a) Adverb
(b) Adjective
(c) Verb
(d) Preposition
Directions (Question No. 11 - 20): Fill in with the correct form of the verb provided at the end of
each question.
11. That you are _________ (drink) while driving, aggravates your offence.
(a) drink
(b) drank
(c) drunk
(d) been drink
12. If your path is being blocked, I _________ (move) my vehicle out of your way.
(a) have moved
(b) will move
(c) moved
(d) moving
13. My uncle Samuel _________ (be) a source of inspiration for me since I was a young boy.
(a) is being
(b) has been
(c) will be
(d) was being
14. Except that Rahul is short-sighted, he is _________.
(a) fit for the post
(b) inept for the post
(c) weak for the post
(d) not eligible for the post
15. If you _________ your eyes you will hurt them.
(a) squeeze
(b) squeezing
(c) squeezed
(d) squeezes
16. Although it _________ (rain) heavily this monsoon, there is a deficit of rainfall in some parts of the
state.
(a) raining
(b) rained
(c) been raining
(d) has been raining
17. In order to save the company from further loss, the employees _________.
(a) formed a union
(b) decided to work extra hours
(c) asked for increase in salary
(d) went on a strike
18. I am busy today. You _________ meet me tomorrow after the class.
(a) Must
(b) Could
(c) Would
(d) Shouldn’t
19. Prakash _________ (wait) at home for an hour but Jaya could not reach on time.
(a) is waiting
(b) will be waiting
(c) had been waiting
(d) has waited
20. I know that you _________ (pass) the exam with flying colours.
(a) pass
(b) will pass
(c) passed
(d) should pass

blank.

(c) customary

(c) few
(d) any

(a) severe
(b) too
(c) much
(d) many
26. Their idea of a holiday _________ at a luxury resort.

(c) is relax
(d) is relaxing

(a) amazing
(b) more amazing
(c) most amazing
(d) as amazing
28. _________ teachers prefer a class that is fairly consistent in having pupils of the same level.
(a) Most
(b) Neither
(c) Whole
(d) Every
29. Tonight we have an appointment at _________ restaurant for a corporate meeting.
(a) big
(b) an big
(c) a big
(d) bigger
30. I lost my _________ shoes.
(a) comfortable
(b) more comfortable
(c) less comfortable
(d) most comfortable
Directions (Question No. 31 - 35): Fill in with the most appropriate adverb to fill in the blanks.
31. We _________ visit our grandparents in winters. They go on pilgrimages then.
(a) usually
(b) never
(c) often
(d) ever
32. Barbie looks _________.
(a) prettily

(b) terrible
(c) more terrible
(d) most terrible

(a) careful
(b) carefully
(c) carefuller
(d) more careful
35. What will be the adverb form of ‘suitable’?
(a) Subtle
(b) Sustain
(c) Suitably
(d) Suited

- 4 -
Directions (Question No. 36 - 40): Fill in with the correct preposition from the given choices.
36. They will appeal _________ your decision.
(a) for
(b) at
(c) against
(d) by
37. The girl was ashamed _________ her misconduct.
(a) at
(b) about
(c) of
(d) with
38. Why don’t you sit _________ me?
(a) close
(b) beside
(c) along
(d) next
39. Entry _________ the building was restricted due to the COVID-19 pandemic.
(a) into
(b) of
(c) for
(d) by
40. Do you know the reason _________ his absence?
(a) on
(b) of
(c) for
(d) none of these

(b) Compound
(c) Complex

(b) Compound
(c) Complex

(b) Compound
(c) Complex

(a) Simple
(b) Compound
(c) Complex
46. The cat astonished everyone by taking part in the ceremony held in honour of the cat’s owner.
(a) Simple
(b) Compound
(c) Complex
47. Nature does not hurry, yet everything is accomplished.
(a) Simple
(b) Compound
(c) Complex
48. While I am a passionate basketball fan, I prefer football.
(a) Simple
(b) Compound
(c) Complex
49. I am working now, but we will eat later. 
(a) Simple
(b) Compound
(c) Complex

- 5 -
50. Jeena was still crying, although she was happy about the news.
(a) Simple
(b) Compound
(c) Complex

(c) Interrogative

57. Do not wash the plates before you use them.
(a) Declarative
(b) Imperative
(c) Interrogative
(d) Exclamatory

59. Could you please pass me the salt and the pepper.

Directions (Question No. 71 - 80): Choose the most suitable meaning of the idioms to make the
sentence meaningful.
71. The dress Mona wore today at the party is in vogue.
(a) never used
(b) out of use
(c) vaguely used
(d) in fashion
72. Mohan is a snake in the grass to his friend Manav.
(a) an unforeseen danger
(b) a secret enemy
(c) an unexpected misfortune
(d) a treacherous person
73. To imagine doing well in business around the area is like a wild goose chase.
(a) to be insensitive to criticism
(b) an absurdly hopeless interprise
(c) a fuss over a trifling matter
(d) to speakboastfully of oneself
74. It’s no use to cry over spilt milk.
(a) complain about a loss or failure
(b) to cry without any reason
(c) to spoil milk
(d) to fight with someone
75. The eldest boy in the family tried to turn the tables when every decision had been made by the father
already.
(a) to welcome
(b) to take revenge
(c) give warning
(d) to reverse the condition
76. My husband seem to have a green thumb.
(a) one’s nails are painted green
(b) to have a natural interest in gardening
(c) one is artistic
(d) one has a tattoo on thumb

(a) in random order
(b) related to fruit packing

(b) puzzled

(a) constantly fighting
(b) associates in some action
(c) suspicious of each other
(d) very close to each other

Directions (Question No. 91 - 100): Choose the correct alternative which is closest in meaning or
is the most appropriate answer to the given sentence.
91. Can you _________ the baby’s cradle, please.
(a) assemble
(b) accemble
(c) assimble
(d) azemble
92. Which of the following options is the closest in meaning to the word ‘primeval’?
(a) Modern
(b) Historic
(c) Primitive
(d) Antique
93. Identify the most appropriate meaning of the word ‘inception’.
(a) Encumber
(b) Skillful
(c) Conceive
(d) Start
94. A ‘sadist’ is one:
(a) who remains sad most of the time
(b) who makes horse saddles
(c) who gets pleasure from hurting others
(d) who wanders from place to place in search
of food

(a) facilitated
(b) felicitated
(c) fantacitated
(d) fecilitated

(c) rogue

(b) controlled
(c) bottled

privacy.

(b) garrulous
(c) salubrious
(d) gregarious
